The GAMA-Bench evaluation (Huang et al., 2025) found that the LLaMA-3.1-405B model underperformed compared to its smaller LLaMA-3.1-70B counterpart. This decreased performance was attributed to the 405B version adopting an "overly conservative strategy" in games like the El Farol Bar. This indicates that a larger model size does not inherently guarantee superior performance in strategic gaming contexts, and specific behavioral biases can lead to suboptimal outcomes.

In contrast, the K-Level Reasoning experiments (Zhang et al., 2025) explored whether a weaker/smaller model, when augmented with a more sophisticated reasoning framework, could outperform a larger, stronger model using direct prompting. Their findings showed that K-R[GPT-3.5] (a GPT-3.5 model utilizing the K-Level Reasoning framework) "outperforms the standard prompting method of GPT-4 (Direct[GPT4]) from average performance" in game-theoretic tasks such as "Guessing 0.8 of the Average" and the "Survival Auction Game." This suggests that an advanced reasoning methodology can significantly enhance the strategic capabilities of even a relatively weaker LLM, enabling it to surpass the performance of a more powerful base model that relies on simpler, direct prompting.

The key contrast lies in the source of performance differences: GAMA-Bench highlights an intrinsic behavioral bias (over-conservatism) in a larger model leading to its underperformance, whereas K-Level Reasoning demonstrates that an enhanced reasoning framework can overcome inherent model strength, allowing a smaller model to achieve superior strategic performance through methodological sophistication.
judge_justification: The response accurately contrasts the two papers: it notes that GAMA-Bench found the larger LLaMA-3.1-405B underperforming the 70B model due to overly conservative behavior, and that K-Level Reasoning showed a smaller/weaker model with the K-R framework (e.g., GPT-3.5) can outperform GPT-4 under direct prompting. It clearly captures the key synthesis that better reasoning methodology can offset scale limitations, while larger size alone does not ensure better strategic performance.
